words.intro: Write a real countdown from **10 to 1**, then make your rocket blast off the stage exactly on zero.
words.finished: That countdown, the colours and the lift-off are all your own Python.
words.tinker: Keep tinkering: count down from 20, change the colours, or make the rocket fly faster.

milestones.title: Count down
milestones.goal: A countdown from 10 to 1, one number every half second.

steps.instruction: Look at `range(10, 0, -1)`. What will this print? Pick your guess, then press **Run**.
steps.explain: `range(10, 0, -1)` starts at **10** and takes steps of **-1**. It stops *before* 0, so the last number is 1. A perfect countdown!
hints: Look at the three numbers inside `range(...)`.
`range(start, stop, step)`: it starts at the first number and stops just before the second one.
It starts at 10, takes steps of -1, and stops before ___.
It prints 10, 9, 8 … down to 1. Pick that answer and press Run.

steps.instruction: A real countdown waits between numbers. Add `stage.wait(0.5)` **inside** the loop, under `print(n)`, so each number waits half a second.

check.description: Tick… tick… tick… a real countdown!

hints: The new line goes inside the for loop, right under `print(n)`.
Lines inside a loop start with 4 spaces. They repeat every time round.
`for i in range(3):` then `    print(i)` then `    stage.wait(1)` waits 1 second after each number.
Under `print(n)`, add a line with 4 spaces, then `stage.wait(___)`.
Add `    stage.wait(0.5)` (4 spaces in front) on the line under `print(n)`.

milestones.title: Numbers on the stage
milestones.goal: Big countdown numbers next to your rocket, turning red at the end.

steps.instruction: Now the rocket stands on the stage. Fill the blank `___` so the stage shows each countdown number. Which variable holds the number?
hints: Look at the `stage.text(320, 130, ___, size=90)` line.
`stage.text(x, y, words)` writes whatever goes in the third spot. The loop keeps the current number in `n`.
`stage.text(320, 130, "Hi", size=90)` would write Hi. You want the number instead.
`stage.text(320, 130, _, size=90)`: the blank is one letter, the loop's variable.
`stage.text(320, 130, n, size=90)`. Type it yourself, then Run.

steps.instruction: New code with `if` and `else`! Which numbers do you think will turn **coral** (orangey-red)?
steps.explain: `if n <= 3:` asks "is n 3 or less?". Only 3, 2 and 1 answer **True**, so they're coral. Every other number goes to `else` and stays cream.

check.description: Watch the last three numbers change colour!

hints: Look at the line `if n <= 3:`.
`<=` means "less than or equal to". The `if` lines run only when that's True.
If n is 7, is 7 <= 3? No, so it goes to `else`.
Only numbers that are 3 or ___ turn coral.
3, 2 and 1 turn coral. Pick that answer and press Run.

steps.instruction: Make the tension start earlier: change the code so the last **five** numbers (5, 4, 3, 2, 1) turn coral.
hints: You only need to change one number, in the `if` line.
`if n <= 3:` is True for 3, 2 and 1. Which number would make it True for 5 down to 1?
`if n <= 7:` would make 7 down to 1 coral.
Change it to `if n <= 5:` and Run.

milestones.title: Lift-off
milestones.goal: The rocket blasts off the top of the stage, with fire underneath.

steps.instruction: Your program now has a lift-off part. `y` is how far down the rocket is. Fill the blank so `y` gets **smaller** every frame and the rocket flies off the top.

check.description: Lift-off! It flew right off the stage!

hints: Look at the line `y = y - ___` near the bottom.
On the stage, y = 0 is the top. To go up, y must get smaller each time round the loop.
`y = y - 5` moves the rocket up 5 steps per frame. That's slow!
`y = y - __`: pick a number big enough to leave the stage in 25 frames.
`y = y - 20`. Try it, then try 30 for a faster rocket.

steps.instruction: Add fire! Inside the lift-off loop, **above** the rocket line, add `stage.sprite("flame", 320, y + 60, 2)`. Want smoke too? Add a `"smoke"` sprite near the ground.
hints: The new line goes inside the second loop (the lift-off one), before `stage.sprite("rocket", ...)`.
Things drawn later go on top. Draw the flame first, then the rocket over it.
`stage.sprite("star", 100, 50)` draws a star at x 100, y 50.
`    stage.sprite("flame", 320, y + __, 2)` with 4 spaces in front.
Add `    stage.sprite("flame", 320, y + 60, 2)` right above `    stage.sprite("rocket", 320, y, 2)`.

milestones.title: Name your rocket
milestones.goal: A launch named by you, for someone you love.

steps.instruction: Every mission needs a name. Change `"Mission Dadi"` to your own, like `"Mission Mama"` or `"Rocket Riff"`. Keep the quotes.
hints: Look for `rocket_name = ` near the top.
Text goes inside quotes. The variable `rocket_name` keeps it for the stage.
`rocket_name = "Mission Nani"` names it after Nani.
`rocket_name = "Mission ______"`
`rocket_name = "Mission Moon"`. Type your own name in, then Run.
